qualifier: This page is for company secretaries who also hold an LLB and want that law degree to carry them into a tech law career.
symptom_title: Two qualifications. One of them does all the work.
symptom: Board meetings, minutes, registers, annual filings, secretarial audits and a compliance calendar that never empties. You keep a company on the right side of its deadlines, and you are trusted to do it.
Your LLB sits beside your CS on the CV, but your job title rarely uses it. Colleagues see you as the person who files, not the person who advises.
You may have thought about using the law degree properly. Litigation feels like starting over, and a corporate law role often looks like more of the same compliance in a bigger office.
outcome_title: Using your LLB as a tech lawyer
outcome: Tech law is legal work for technology companies, mostly contracts, privacy, compliance and disputes. Moving into it puts your law degree at the front. You would work as a lawyer on privacy programmes, company structuring and tech policies, for startups, firm tech teams or tech companies.
Your compliance discipline comes with you, but the role changes. Instead of tracking someone else's legal work, you would be the lawyer doing it.
alternatives_title: What CS and LLB holders often try

alternatives.t: Adding another certificate to the CV
alternatives.why: Each new course sits beside the others. None of them changes how employers read your profile, which is still compliance first.

alternatives.t: Moving to a bigger company as CS
alternatives.why: The board is larger and the filings are more complex. The role, and how far your LLB is used, stays the same.

alternatives.t: Applying for legal roles with no legal work to show
alternatives.why: Hiring managers ask what you have drafted or advised on. A strong compliance record does not answer that question.

reframe_title: Your compliance habit is the asset. Your LLB is the licence to use it.
reframe: Tech companies carry a long list of duties: privacy compliance, sector filings, sandbox applications, and the duties platforms owe for what their users post. The script calls compliance work recurring. Tracking recurring duties is your trade. A CS already knows what it takes to keep a company in good standing year after year, and tech companies need that rhythm applied to privacy and platform rules.

So the move is a matter of positioning, not of working harder. You already think like a compliance lawyer. What you need is the tech vocabulary, a few legal documents in your own name, and an introduction that leads with the LLB.
cost_title: If the LLB stays in the second line
cost: Staying put is safe, and your CS work is valued. The cost is that the law degree you worked hard for keeps waiting, while privacy and tech compliance work goes to lawyers who said yes to it first.
role_h2: What tech law work looks like for a company secretary with an LLB
role: Privacy work is the most natural start. The 6-month plan begins with the easiest skills: DPDP, GDPR, policies and contracts. You would map how a company collects and uses personal data, draft the privacy policy, and keep its privacy duties on a calendar.

Structuring is the second fit. Founders ask whether a business can be done, where and at what cost. On Day 3 the camp structures a blockchain venture as a Wyoming DAO LLC, and the plan includes foreign investment and international expansion.

You would also handle the compliance side of fintech and e-commerce companies: sector filings, sandbox applications and the policies a platform must publish. This is legal advice, not filing support, and your LLB is what lets you give it.
first_artifact: On Day 3 we build an Upwork profile as a data protection lawyer with you: a 3-part headline, an introduction, services, availability and a video CV. We also walk through structuring a Wyoming company for a blockchain founder. You leave with a profile that introduces you as a privacy lawyer, which is the first time many CS and LLB holders lead with the law degree.
longer_term: The plan is about 2 hours a day: 1 hour learning and 1 hour on outreach and track record. Starting with privacy and policies, then adding structuring and tech compliance, you could build a set of legal work samples over 6 months. That could support an application to a tech company's legal team or a practice of your own. Privacy is a sensible first skill because it builds on what you already do every week.

faq.q: Is this for company secretaries or for lawyers?
faq.a: It is for lawyers. You qualify because you hold an LLB, and the page speaks to that degree. Your CS experience is the head start.

faq.q: I have never practised in court. Does that matter?
faq.a: No. Tech law here is drafting, compliance, privacy and structuring work. The camp teaches it through documents, not court practice.

faq.q: Will I need to understand technology deeply?
faq.a: No. The script says the work follows how a business makes money and needs no coding or science background.

closing_title: Company secretaries with an LLB: put your law degree to work in tech law
closing: Company secretaries who hold an LLB already know compliance better than most lawyers. In 3 live evenings, 24 to 26 Oct, we show how that skill and your law degree could become a tech law career in privacy, structuring and tech compliance.
